summary: Mrs. Bensadon discusses the thematic shift in Sefer Vayikra from the Mishkan-centered service of the Kohanim to the laws governing daily life in Parashat Aharei Mot and Kedoshim. She explains that holiness is not limited to the Mishkan but must be integrated into everyday actions, business dealings, and social justice. By contrasting the service of Aharon with the actions of Nadav and Avihu, she emphasizes the importance of maintaining a proper, commanded relationship with Hashem in all aspects of life.
questions: Why does the Torah repeat the story of the death of Nadav and Avihu in Parashat Aharei Mot?
How does the Torah's definition of holiness differ from common misconceptions?
Why does the focus of Sefer Vayikra shift from the Mishkan to daily life?
What is the significance of the cloud and the fire in the service of the Kohen Gadol?
How can we apply the lessons of the Mishkan to our mundane daily activities?
